A few things I do outside of math.

::: {.section-block}
## City Streets

I am interested in how much one can learn about a city just by looking at its
streets. The starting point is
[Geoff Boeing](https://geoffboeing.com/)'s work on
[urban street network orientation](https://geoffboeing.com/2019/09/urban-street-network-orientation/),
which measures how close a city is to a grid by the entropy of its street
bearings.

City Streets extends this to three dimensions. Crossing compass bearing with
grade, each city's street network defines a probability measure on
$\mathbb{RP}^2$. From these measures I compute rotation-aligned Wasserstein and
Jensen–Shannon distances between 84 cities, along with measures of hilliness,
walkability, on-street parking, and staircase streets. The project is a Julia
package with an interactive dashboard.

[Open the dashboard](/city-streets/) ·
[More about the project](projects/city-streets.qmd)
:::

::: {.section-block}
## Leatherwork

I make small goods out of vegetable-tanned leather, mostly wallets and belts,
cutting and saddle-stitching each piece by hand. One of the things I like about
being in Chicago is that the
[Horween Leather Company](https://www.horween.com/) is here.

## Boots

I wear and care for heritage boots. What interests me is patina, meaning the way
a pair takes on the shape and markings of the person wearing it over time.

<div class="award">
